newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares close weaker on profit taking, Dow.
newsitem.headline: KL shares close weaker on profit taking, Dow.

text.p: Shares closed weaker as investors booked in profits after a four-day winning run, dealers and analysts said.
The overnight fall of Wall Street and still-fragile local sentiments caused sellers to dominate as buyers stayed sidelined, they said.

"Sentiment is not good, so people are just profit taking," said Phuah Lee Kerk, head of research at Jupiter Securities. "There are people who think the market has hit the bottom but sentiment is still not there," he said. The key Composite Index fell 7.10 points or 0.63 percent to close at 1,120.50.
The broader Emas Index fell 3.42 points or 1.06 percent to 320.57.
"There's no buying interest though there's no bad news whatsoever. I expect this to continue for some time," said an institutional dealer at a Malaysian brokerage.
The dearth of fresh local incentives has led the market to track the movements of the Dow, analysts said. The Dow on Monday fell 43.34 points to 6,660.21.
Stocks which were fast risers on bargain hunting activities gave back some of their gains.
